"), located in Cibola and McKinley Counties, New Mexico, USA, through NM Energy.

The acquisition represents an important advancement of Americas Uranium's strategy to build a portfolio of uranium assets in North America and provides the Company with an exploration property containing known uranium mineralization, historical drilling and multiple opportunities for resource confirmation and expansion.
Transaction and Project Highlights
100% Interest in Treeline:
Americas Uranium will acquire a 100% interest in the Treeline Property and associated property rights, subject to existing and newly granted royalties.
Historical Estimate of 1.02 Million Pounds U
O

Historical information relating to the Treeline Property includes an estimate of approximately 1,020,000 pounds of U₃O₈. This estimate was calculated in 1978 and there are insufficient details available on the procedures used to determine if any of this estimate meets National Instrument 43-101 ("

") standards (Penn and Rice, 2005). The historical estimate predates the Company's interest in the Property. A qualified person has not completed sufficient work to classify the historical estimate as a current mineral resource or mineral reserve, and the Company is not treating the historical estimate as a current mineral resource or mineral reserve. Additional work will be required to verify and update historical estimates, including a review of the assumptions, parameters, methods, and testing. See "Historical Uranium Estimate" below for more details.
Two Known Uranium Trends:

Uranium mineralization is concentrated within the North and South trends. Historical information indicates that the North trend extends approximately 2,000 feet northwest-southeast and is approximately 175 feet wide, while the South trend extends approximately 3,250 feet and ranges from approximately 50 to 150 feet in width.
Relatively Shallow Mineralization:
Axiom Exploration Group's ("
Axiom
") review of the historical data notes that both zones of mineralization are relatively shallow, providing a potentially favorable setting for future drilling and evaluation.
Established Uranium District:

The Property is located in Cibola and McKinley Counties, New Mexico, in an area with a history of uranium exploration and mining. Historical mining has occurred immediately southeast of the Property at the San Mateo mine.
Defined Path Toward Modern Resource Evaluation:

Axiom recommends compiling and digitizing historical drilling, developing an updated geological and resource model, and conducting RC and diamond drilling, gamma logging and twin drilling a selection of historic drill holes to determine the work required to potentially establish a new NI 43-101-compliant mineral resource.
Additional Exploration Potential:

Axiom has identified exploration potential along the North and South trends, including areas north and south of the San Mateo mine and east-southeast along trend. The Company advises that, notwithstanding their proximity of location, discoveries of minerals at the San Mateo mine and any promising results thereof are not necessarily indicative of the mineralization of, or located on the Treeline Property or the Company's ability to commercially exploit the Treeline Property or to locate any commercially exploitable deposits therefrom.
Attractive Acquisition Structure:
Consideration consists of US$100,000 in cash (the "
Cash Payment
") and C$2,000,000 in common shares of Americas Uranium (each, a "
Share
" and together, the "
Shares
"), with 90% of the share consideration payable in staged issuances over the 36 months following closing.
Strategic Expansion Rights:
Americas Uranium will also receive a right of first refusal over specified additional properties surrounding the acquired land position.
Treeline Uranium Property

The Treeline Property is located in Cibola and McKinley Counties, New Mexico, and consists of a combination of unpatented mining claims, fee mineral rights and certain leased surface and mineral rights.

According to the historical technical information reviewed by Axiom, uranium mineralization in the area is hosted primarily within the Westwater Canyon Member sandstone and Poison Canyon sandstone. All known uranium mineralization identified on the Treeline Property occurs within the Poison Canyon sandstone, making this sandstone package an important target for future exploration.

Historical exploration identified two principal mineralized trends, referred to as the North Trend and South Trend. The North Trend is reported to extend approximately 2,000 feet from northwest to southeast and to be approximately 175 feet wide. The South Trend is reported to extend approximately 3,250 feet along strike and range from approximately 50 to 150 feet in width.

Axiom notes that both zones of mineralization are relatively shallow and that most known historical drilling was conducted within the lease lands in Section 24, which contains both the North and South trends. Historical drilling was also conducted southeast of Section 24 near the workings of the San Mateo mine. Historical uranium mining has occurred in the surrounding area, including at San Mateo and the nearby Chill Wills mine.
Historical Uranium Estimate

Following its review of the "Technical Report of the Treeline Project, Cibola and McKinley Counties, New Mexico, USA" prepared by Neil Prenn, P.E. and John A. Rice, CPG and dated January 10, 2005 (the "
Report
"), Axiom concluded that the Property has exploration potential and noted that a historical resource exists on the Property.

Historical information relating to the Treeline Property includes an estimate of approximately 1,020,000 pounds of U₃O₈. The historical estimate from 1978 was summarized in the Report. Historical estimates do not use the current mineral resource categories prescribed under NI 43-101. There are insufficient details available on the procedures used in these estimates to determine if any portion meets NI 43-101 standards or to draw any comparisons to current CIM Definition Standards. To the QP's knowledge there are not more recent resource estimates for the Treeline Property.

The Company considers the historical estimate relevant because it provides an indication of uranium mineralization identified by historical drilling and may assist the Company in planning future exploration of the Property. The Company and its Qualified Person consider the historical estimate to be reliable for the limited purposes of exploration planning.
Exploration and Resource Advancement Strategy

Axiom's review concluded that the Treeline Property has geological merit due to the uranium mineralization historically identified within Section 24 and recommends that future exploration initially focus on determining the work necessary to establish a current NI 43-101-compliant resource, including:
Compilation and digitization of all known historical drill holes;
Development of an updated geological and resource model;
RC and diamond core drilling;
Gamma logging to enable comparison with historical drill-hole information;
Twinning of selected historical holes along both the North and South trends;
Collection and analysis of drill cuttings and core using modern analytical techniques; and
Additional exploration along extensions of the North and South trends.

Axiom also identified additional exploration potential east-southeast along trend on the unpatented mining claims and in areas north and south of the San Mateo mine. The Company intends to undertake a comprehensive review and compilation of the available historical database following completion of the acquisition and use the results to design its initial exploration program.
U.S. Uranium and Nuclear Energy Market Context
The acquisition of the Treeline Property comes at a time of renewed investment and activity across the U.S. uranium and nuclear energy sectors.

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, U.S. uranium mine production increased to approximately 1.4 million pounds of U3O8 in 2025, approximately double the 0.7 million pounds reported in 2024 and the highest annual level since 2016.(1)

During 2025, U.S. uranium exploration drilling totaled approximately 1.016 million feet across 1,824 holes. U.S. uranium industry employment increased 41% to 711 full-time person-years, while industry expenditures for land, exploration, drilling, production and reclamation reached approximately US$234.7 million.(1)

In May 2025, the U.S. Administration established a policy objective of increasing American nuclear generating capacity from approximately 100 gigawatts in 2024 to 400 gigawatts by 2050.(2) In June 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy announced a US$17.5 billion conditional loan commitment intended to support procurement of long-lead components for 10 new AP1000 nuclear reactors and potentially accelerate their deployment by up to three years. (3)

The Company believes these developments highlight the increasing strategic importance of domestic uranium exploration and development as the United States seeks to expand nuclear generating capacity and strengthen domestic nuclear fuel supply chains.
Management Commentary
Nicholas Luksha, President and Chief Executive Officer of Americas Uranium Corp., commented:

The acquisition of Treeline represents an important step for Americas Uranium as we build a portfolio of uranium assets in North America. With a historical estimate of approximately 1.02 million pounds of U
O
, known uranium mineralization and historical exploration, Treeline provides a solid foundation for further exploration."

As the U.S. expands nuclear power and strengthens its domestic nuclear fuel supply chain, we believe high-quality American uranium assets will become increasingly important. Our focus is now on advancing the historical work at Treeline and determining the drilling required to evaluate the historical estimate under current NI 43-101 standards."

The Property is also subject to an existing 2% net proceeds royalty on uranium and 2% net smelter returns royalty on other minerals pursuant to a May 15, 2025 royalty deed between Verdera and enCore Energy Corp.
Right of First Refusal Provides Additional Expansion Opportunity

As part of the transaction, Americas Uranium will receive a right of first refusal over specified additional property interests in the surrounding area should Verdera seek to sell or transfer such interests. The additional property encompasses specified sections within Townships 13 North, Ranges 8 West and 9 West, potentially providing Americas Uranium with an opportunity to further consolidate its land position around the Treeline Property.
Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information regarding the Treeline Property contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Troy Marfleet, P.Geo. of Axiom, Technical Advisor for the Company, and a Qualified Person as defined by NI 43-101.

The technical information regarding the historical estimate is based upon historical information reviewed by Axiom, including the Report. The historical estimate does not meet current NI 43-101 requirements, and the Company is not treating it as a current mineral resource or mineral reserve.
About Americas Uranium Corp.

Americas Uranium Corp. is a uranium exploration company focused on the acquisition, exploration and advancement of uranium projects in the Americas, with an emphasis on assets positioned to contribute to the growing need for secure North American uranium supply. The Company's common shares trade in Canada under the symbol NUCA, in the United States under the symbol ASRFF, and in Germany under the symbol WA7.
